resources.string: Enable controls for this app, then choose a preset or tune individual settings. You do not need to raise every slider.
Applied while this app is in the foreground. Leaving the app or turning the screen off restores normal touch behavior.
The global responsiveness option takes priority. Your per-app settings are saved but paused. Tap here to manage the global option.
The touch service did not provide valid control ranges. Reopen this page to retry.
A preset replaces response, sensitivity, aim and tap stability together. Manual settings stay saved for later. Edge protection works separately in either mode.
Adjust tap response. 0 restores the firmware default; change one setting at a time and test it in your game.
Adjust touch sensitivity. 0 restores the firmware default; a higher level is not automatically better for every game.
Fine-tune aiming gestures only if needed. 0 restores the firmware default.
Fine-tune repeated-tap stability only if needed. 0 restores the firmware default.
0 disables edge filtering; levels 1–3 increase protection against accidental edge touches. Stronger filtering can make intentional edge touches harder.
Return to manual firmware defaults and the default edge protection. Keep the app’s enable switch unchanged.

Start with manual defaults. Enable tuning only for apps that need it.

Presets and manual adjustments are alternatives, not effects to stack. Presets 1–3 are firmware profiles; they are not quality ratings.

In manual mode, 0 restores the firmware default. Higher levels change the touch behavior and may feel worse in some games. Adjust response or sensitivity first; use aim and stability only for finer tuning.

Edge filtering is independent. Stronger protection can also reject intentional touches near the screen edge.

The global responsiveness option takes priority over per-app tuning. These controls do not change the display refresh rate.
